fine_trace.note: The parser option XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE from the input enables reader-side XInclude processing when the reader reaches an attacker supplied xi:include element.
The current xi:include node is expanded and handed to the XInclude processor while the reader still holds traversal state for the same document tree.
The first phase discovers each attacker supplied XInclude node and queues it for later replacement in the context.
The queued include reference stores a raw xmlNodePtr pointing at the source xi:include node, so later phases depend on that node remaining live.
The replacement phase reloads the saved raw pointer for an include entry without verifying that an earlier replacement in the same context has not freed that node.
With XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE-style replacement the original include node is unlinked and freed after included content is inserted, invalidating any saved references to that node.
A subsequent include replacement dereferences the stale saved node pointer to read cur->type, producing the heap-use-after-free reported in xmlXIncludeIncludeNode.
